title: ENDEX: Sunday 13:30, Galveston Turnaround

fields.resolution: ENDEX. It is 22:00 on the exercise clock, four hours after STARTEX, and in the story it is about 13:30 Central on Sunday, February 21, 2027, with MV Halcyon Dawn alongside at the Port of Galveston. The chlorine mixing station is back at a verified 1,000 ppm on the adapted dosing pump. The 180 re-done cabins from P-9000 are signed off, and cabin and public-area cleaning continues on the timeline shoreside chose. The next voyage is held or boarding under the option and times announced at 10:00, plus any extension since. No guest boards before the VSP has reviewed the records and the Environmental Officer has done the walk-through. This concludes the exercise.
finalState: The signed count that every channel should carry is the 07:00 medical log entry, signed by the CMO at 07:15: 121 passengers (4.1% of 2,980) and 32 crew (2.9% of 1,120), cumulative since embarkation, plus 1 death on board, cause unknown.

Booked guests, travel agents, the national travel association, Gulf Terminal Services, the Port of Galveston, the Galveston County Health District, Texas DSHS and the Galveston and Houston TV desks have been given the boarding decision.
The family hotline script has been revised to cover the boarding status and the death on board.
Cabin P-8417 stays sealed. The VSP team is still on board reviewing records and sampling the galley and the Lido.
Public areas, the medical center, the Deck 2 forward isolation cabins and the terminal are still being cleaned. Nothing goes into an attestation that has not been verified.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Exercise play stops here. Put down the phones, radios and drafts, and don't throw away any notes. Take five minutes to write down the time of every decision and every report you made, and every number you sent out on any channel. Then we start the hot wash.
fields.hotWashMethod: Timeline reconstruction against the documents: each role posts its decision and report times on one shared timeline, which we then compare with HOPRPG 5 to 8, HR-HSP-02 5 to 6 and HR-COM-03 4 to 7. After that, 3-Up, 3-Down for each role.
hotWashQuestions: Did every report go out on its own clock and from the signed log: the 2 percent and 3 percent special reports, the 24-hour report between 19:00 Friday and 07:00 Saturday, the 4-hour update by 03:00 Sunday, and the immediate death report to the Houston quarantine station?

Did the media statement, the hotline, the guest letter, the crew notice and the partner messages ever give different numbers, or different times for the count? If they did, where did the second number come from?

Was the boarding decision made by 10:00? Was every line of the attestation backed by verified cleaning records, including the unsigned Lido round, the 4-hourly entries and the batches that failed at 620 ppm?
Where did the steward, gown and laundry limits force a trade-off? Who made that call, and was it written down?
How did we balance the family's request for time with the media deadlines and the required reports about Guest A?
fields.facilitatorNote: Collect role logs, draft reports, the draft attestation and any statement drafts before the break. Under HOPRPG 9, the hot wash must be held within 72 hours of arrival and the written report filed within 14 days, with corrective actions in the fleet's action tracker. Note who owns each gap.
fields.scenarioTitle: Same Count, Every Channel — Norovirus Thresholds, Reporting & Turnaround

instructorNote: This card closes play. Make sure every role records its decision and report times and any counts that didn't match between channels before discussion starts, so the hot wash can test the gaps against HOPRPG 5 to 8, HR-HSP-02 5 to 6 and HR-COM-03 4 to 7. Watch for teams that remember sending the 07:00 count everywhere when their drafts show older figures, such as the 4-hour update with 'since last report' numbers typed into the cumulative field.
